newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: Banco Espirito boosts solvability ratio.
newsitem.headline: Banco Espirito boosts solvability ratio.

text.p: Recent capital operations launched by Banco Espirito Santo (BES), involving some 74 billion escudos of subordinate bonds, have raised its solvability ratio to 14 percent from 10.7 percent, the bank said.
The ratio was based on the Bank for International Settlements ' (BIS) definition. The relative figures on the Bank of Portugal's definition would be 12.3 percent against 8.9 percent, previously.
The bank said the capital operations, which involved three subordinated bond issues, were also aimed at helping finance its programme of "organic" growth.

"The decision to reinforce shareholder assets had a double intention. First to strength (us) financially, and secondly to support the strategy of organic growth of the BES group," it said in a statement.
BES is one of the few major Portuguese banks not to seek to expand through a policy of acquisitions.
The bank noted that the minimum solvability ratio set by the Bank of Portugal was eight percent.
